difficulty_reason: The selected global linear bound uses endpoint rotations to extract a small-neighborhood set and charges a new separating family only to the removed vertices, rather than carrying an iterated-logarithmic cost through induction. Its new core constructs actual simple paths through nested chords by backward induction and combines two independent endpoint-index partitions to distinguish every ordered edge pair. Even with the precisely stated ordinary Pósa and Dean–Kouider inputs, those nonroutine constructions and the full 19n budget remain substantive research-level obligations of the main theorem, not routine auxiliary claims.
